stem: A quality-improvement team is reviewing a medication-administration error and chooses the IHI 5 Whys tool. Which action best demonstrates use of this method?

options.A: Ask why repeatedly, using each answer to probe the next causal layer until the team reaches the underlying cause or causes
options.B: Map the process and identify possible failure modes before another adverse event occurs
options.C: Plot error rates over time to distinguish common-cause from special-cause variation
options.D: Test a small workflow change, study the results, and adapt the next test based on what is learned

rationale: IHI describes the 5 Whys as repeatedly asking why an event occurred and continuing to ask why based on successive answers until the underlying root cause is reached; IHI also notes that a problem may have more than one root cause. Therefore A is the best answer. B describes the proactive logic of Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), C describes use of a control chart to examine process variation over time, and D describes a Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycle for testing change. Each distractor is a legitimate quality-improvement method, but none is the 5 Whys technique.
educational_objective: Differentiate the 5 Whys root-cause technique from other quality-improvement methods by recognizing its repeated causal questioning from an observed problem toward underlying causes.
source_version_date: Current undated IHI web tool page; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Main page text and section 'Ask Why? Five Times': ask 'Why did this happen?' and continue asking 'Why?' again and again until reaching the root cause; page also notes that a problem may have multiple root causes
source_claim_supported: The 5 Whys technique identifies underlying root causes by repeatedly asking why successive causal explanations occurred; multiple root causes may exist.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.25: define performance improvement/quality assurance activities; participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; utilize research and other references for performance improvement actions
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement) / root-cause analysis tool selection
correction_summary: Replaced the source item's simple definition recall and weak distractors with an applied quality-improvement scenario. Kept the verified 5 Whys construct, removed wording implying that exactly five questions are always mandatory, and used three real alternative QI methods as plausible distractors.
audit_findings: Correct answer A is directly supported by the current IHI 5 Whys page. IHI's FMEA tool supports B as a proactive process-failure analysis method rather than 5 Whys; IHI's control-chart guidance supports C as analysis of common- versus special-cause variation; IHI's PDSA guidance supports D as iterative testing of change. No distractor is absurd, no option overlaps the defining action of 5 Whys, and no second answer remains. The wording avoids turning the name 'Five Whys' into an absolute requirement that exactly five questions must always be asked. The item is directly relevant to NCSBN 2026 Management of Care performance-improvement content and is appropriate at medium difficulty because the candidate must discriminate among four legitimate QI methods.
